summary: Richard von Glahn is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. He was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo (1988–1989) and became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist. She completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki under supervisors Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Komazawa University (~1962–1972), where he later served as lecturer (~1978) and Professor of Buddhist Studies until 1997.
Ringu Tulku is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and under traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Rinzin Thargyal worked in Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo in 1985, studying under supervisor Fredrik Barth and temporary supervisor Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004 under Lambert Schmithausen), later holding a post at the University of Bristol.

Rita M. Gross was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at the University of Chicago (~1965–1975) and served at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 1990) and University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire (~1979–2007).
Rizong Rinpoche was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College from around 1979 to 1985.

Rob Linrothe specializes in art history, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Chicago (~1982–1992) and held academic posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Zimbabwe (~1957–1960) and the University of London/King's College London (~1960–1964). He held posts at the University of Zimbabwe (~1965–1970) and the University of Cape Town (~1970–1980).

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1967–1972) and held posts at Amherst College (1973) and Columbia University (1988).

Robert Aitken was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied under Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki, at the University of Hawaii, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji, and later held a post at the University of Hawaii.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD in 2002 at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetologist. He served at the University of Chicago (~1953–1958), the University of Washington (1958), and as honorary curator of Asian ethnology at the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (~1973–1983).
Robert Barnett is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied at the University of Cambridge from ~1972 to 1976 and served as a professor at Columbia University from ~1999 to 2018.

Robert Caesar Childers was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Wadham College and under Yataramulle Dhammarama, later serving as Professor of Pali and Buddhist Literature at University College London and University of London (~1872–1876).
Robert Chalmers was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Oriel College (~1877–1881) and served as Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge (~1924–1931).

Robert Chambers was an Indology scholar who studied at Lincoln College (~1754–1758). He held posts at the University of Oxford (~1766–1773), the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (~1789–1798), and the Asiatic Society (~1797–1798).

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. After studying at Christ Church (~1933–1937) and serving in the Secret Intelligence Service (~1943–1952), he was Spalding Professor at Oxford (~1952–1974).

Robert DeCaroli is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA under Robert L. Brown and Katherine Anne Harper, and joined the faculty at George Mason University around 1999.
